places.name: Seminyak
places.description: Bali's upscale coastal village — boutique hotels, sunset beach clubs, and designer villas set behind a long black-sand surf beach facing the Indian Ocean.
highlights: Potato Head Beach Club — Bali's most iconic sunset venue
Jalan Kayu Aya boutique fashion and homeware strip
Weekend artisan market at La Plancha on the sand
Direct beach access from the village centre

places.name: Kuta Beach
places.description: Bali's legendary surf beach and the island's beating heart — a 2km stretch of sand backed by surf schools, warungs, and a vibrant backpacker and surf scene.
highlights: Consistent right-hand surf break — ideal for beginners
Classic Kuta sunset with the widest beach view in southern Bali
Legian night market on the coastal road after dark
10-minute drive from Ngurah Rai International Airport

places.name: Canggu
places.description: Bali's most creative village — rice field co-working spaces, a surf break watched by water buffaloes, and the island's densest collection of specialty coffee shops.
highlights: Batu Bolong Beach — local surf break with warung front-row seats
Rice paddy walking trails from Pererenan to Seseh
Canggu Club swimming lagoon — colonial-era sports club
Highest specialty coffee shop density per kilometre on Bali

places.name: Ubud
places.description: Bali's cultural capital — ancient royal palace, traditional Kecak dance every night, the Sacred Monkey Forest, and terraced rice fields in every direction.
highlights: Puri Saren Agung Royal Palace — nightly Kecak dance performances
Sacred Monkey Forest Sanctuary — 1,000+ macaques in a living Hindu temple
Tegalalang rice terraces — Bali's most photographed landscape
Jalan Raya Ubud market — traditional offerings, textiles, and stone carvings

places.name: Tanah Lot
places.description: Bali's most dramatic sea temple — a 16th-century Hindu shrine perched on a tidal rock formation, surrounded by crashing waves and silhouetted against the sunset.
highlights: 16th-century Pura Tanah Lot on its own rock island
Accessible on foot at low tide — waves close the crossing at high tide
Sunset from the clifftop viewpoint — Bali's most photographed image
Surrounding clifftop with smaller shrines and flower offering stalls

places.name: Tegallalang Rice Terraces
places.description: Bali's most iconic landscape — a series of emerald staircase rice paddies carved into a river valley north of Ubud, using the ancient subak irrigation cooperative system recognised by UNESCO.
highlights: UNESCO-listed subak irrigation system still in active use
Sunrise visit: mist fills the valley below the terraces before 07:30
Swing overlooking the valley — viral viewpoint with 360° paddy view
Roadside warungs serving Balinese breakfast with a paddy panorama

places.name: Sanur Sunrise Walk
places.description: Sanur is Bali's only east-facing beach resort — the 4km coastal path catches the sunrise over the Lombok Strait while the rest of Bali faces sunset. Traditional jukung outrigger boats line the calm lagoon at dawn.
highlights: East-facing beach: the only Bali sunrise on sand (all others face west)
Sanur Boardwalk — 4km continuous coastal pedestrian promenade
Jukung outrigger fleet at anchor in the lagoon at dawn
Warung breakfast culture: nasi jinggo and Bali coffee from 06:00
